correctness.rationale: The source's exact negative-energy polynomial is affine in \(Q=\cos\theta_1+\cos\theta_2\). Collecting the \(Q\)-terms gives exactly \(2\kappa(1+\kappa^2)\sinh(\kappa\ell)\), strictly positive for every \(\kappa,\ell>0\). Hence a fixed negative energy can occur only on one analytic level set of \(Q\), which has two-dimensional torus measure zero. The hyperbolic reduction has no omitted Dirichlet singularity because \(\sinh(\kappa\ell)\neq0\). The symbolic verifier reconstructs the identity exactly.

value.rationale: The primary source makes the phase dependence of transport and flat-band persistence a central feature, explicitly derives a separate negative-energy Floquet equation, and studies negative bands. Establishing that the entire negative sector has no point component for every edge length and every interior phase closes a natural structural question: any negative spectral component is necessarily dispersive rather than an infinitely degenerate localized level. This is global in parameters and is not implied by the source's positive flat-band example or by large-edge negative-band asymptotics.
